text: Beloved means loved very, very much. Kids have loved this bear for 100 years.
To illustrate a book is to draw its pictures. Ernest H. Shepard drew the pictures of Pooh.
To charm someone is to make them smile and like you very much. The Pooh stories charm readers.
Winnie-the-Pooh is a kind, silly bear in a famous children's book. He loves honey.
Turns 100 means will be 100 years old. The book came out in 1926.
Willy-nilly means in a mixed-up, silly way, with no plan.
Hunny is how Pooh spells honey. It is a funny spelling on purpose.
Published means a book was printed and shared so people could read it.
A.A. Milne was the author who wrote the Pooh stories.
Ernest H. Shepard was the artist who drew the pictures of Pooh.
Christopher Robin is the boy in the stories. He is Pooh's best friend.
Based on means made from something real. The character came from a real boy.
A stuffed animal is a soft toy that looks like an animal.
The London Zoo is a zoo in London, a big city in England.
Winnipeg was a real bear at the zoo. Christopher named his toy Winnie after her.
Renamed means gave a new name.
A swan is a big white bird with a long neck. It swims on ponds.
The Hundred Acre Wood is the forest where Pooh and his friends live in the stories.
Ashdown Forest is a real forest in England. It gave the author the idea for the Hundred Acre Wood.
England is a country. It is part of the United Kingdom.
Walt Disney started a company that makes cartoons and movies.
Animated means made into a cartoon, with drawings that seem to move.
Here, a short is a very short movie.
The New York Public Library is a big library in New York City. People can borrow books there.
A director is a person in charge of a group of workers.
To celebrate is to show that something is special and fun.
A display is a show of things set out so people can look at them.
